newsitem.title: USA: Mercantile of St. Louis in $1 billion acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Mercantile of St. Louis in $1 billion acquisition.

text.p: Mercantile Bancorporation Inc. said Monday it reached a definitive agreement to acquire Roosevelt Financial Group, Inc. for $1 billion.
In a joint statement, the companies said the combined institition will create the largest locally managed and independently owned financial services organisation based in the lower Midwest.
The acquisition positions Mercantile as the largest financial institution in Missouri, with more than 23 percent of the state's deposits, Mercantile said.

Mercantile will become the largest bank in the St. Louis and Springfield, Mo., markets, the second-largest institution in Kansas City and will strengthen its presence in a number of other major Missouri markets.
Roosevelt, a $9 billion thrift holding company, is based in St. Louis, with 81 locations in Missouri, Kansas and Illinois.

"Our combination with Roosevelt will materially enhance our mix of strong retail, middle market lending and other speciality businesses," said Thomas H. Jacobsen, Mercantile's chairman. "As the leading mortgage originator and servicer in Missouri, Mercantile will enter the top tier of mortgage providers nationwide," Jacobsen added.

The acquisition comes two months after Mercantile agreed to buy another Missouri banking company, Mark Twain Bancshares, with $3.1 billion in assets, for $855 million in stock. That merger is pending.
The Mercantile that emerges as a result of all pending mergers will be an organisation with $30 billion in assets and a market capitalisation in excess of $4 billion, it said.
Mercantile said it will exchange up to 13 million shares of its common stock at a ratio 0.4211 Mercantile share for each Roosevelt share, and pay $22 cash for the remaining shares.

Based on the $50.75 closing price Friday of Mercantile's shares on the New York Stock Exchange, the exchange ratio would value Roosevelt shares at $21.37 each. Roosevelt's stock closed Friday at $18.125 on Nasdaq.
Mercantile also said it plans to repurchase up to 7 million of its own shares in connection with the acquisition.

Following the completion of the merger, Stanley J. Bradshaw, chairman of Roosevelt, will lead the combined mortgage operations and become a member of Mercantile's management executive committee reporting to Jacobsen.
Plans call for the merger, which is subject to the approval of Roosevelt shareholders and all appropriate regulatory agencies, to be completed in mid-1997.
